subject: Accounting
pacing_note: The IEB publishes no ATP equivalent; term placement and week spans are the DBE ATP pacing carried over as a default. IEB schools set their own pacing — treat weeks as advisory.
assessment_note: DBE SBA programmes, control-test scopes and exam structures are deliberately stripped: IEB assessment is specified by the IEB Subject Assessment Guidelines (see ../exam_guidelines/), which have not been ingested yet. Do not fall back to the CAPS exam_structure for IEB papers.
scope_deltas: SAG-stated content-scope differences vs the CAPS/DBE prescription are recorded in scope_deltas.json in this folder (hand-maintained, SAG-transcribed only; an empty ledger means 'not yet transcribed', never 'no differences').

topics.name: RECONCILIATION
subtopics: Bank reconciliation: reconcile bank statements with cash journals; stop/debit orders, EFTs, bank charges, interest, corrections; outstanding deposits and EFTs
Creditors reconciliation: reconcile creditors' monthly statements with the creditors ledger; outstanding invoices, credit notes, payments, unrecorded discounts, corrections
Integrate ethics and internal control; apply GAAP
topics.prior_knowledge: Gr 10: cash journals and bank-account posting; creditors (CJ, CAJ, creditors control and ledger); control-account vs list reconciliations

topics.name: FIXED ASSETS
subtopics: Need for and compilation of a fixed/tangible asset register
Record acquisition of fixed assets
Depreciation: straight-line and diminishing balance; fully depreciated assets
Disposal of fixed assets (cash, credit, trade-in, donated, owner's drawings) at beginning/during/end of the year
Ethics and internal control over movement and use of fixed assets
topics.prior_knowledge: Gr 10 transactions for acquiring fixed assets and depreciation calculations

topics.name: FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING OF PARTNERSHIPS: ADJUSTMENTS, LEDGER, ACCOUNTING EQUATION, FINAL ACCOUNTS
subtopics: Partnership concepts: capital and current accounts, interest on capital, salaries and bonuses to partners, distribution of profits/losses
IFRS and GAAP principles (historical cost, prudence, materiality, business entity, going concern, matching)
Partnership accounting cycle: documents, journals, ledgers, trial balance, final accounts; accounting-equation analysis
Year-end adjustments (revision) plus new: provision for bad debts, capitalised interest on loan
Partnership-agreement adjustments; trading, profit and loss, and appropriation accounts
Reversal of accruals, deferred income and prepayments at the start of the next period
topics.prior_knowledge: Partnerships as a form of ownership; Gr 10 accounting cycle, year-end adjustments and final accounts

topics.name: PARTNERSHIPS: FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND NOTES
subtopics: Statement of comprehensive income, statement of financial position and notes
Apply IFRS and GAAP principles
topics.prior_knowledge: Gr 10 IFRS/GAAP principles, year-end adjustments, accounting cycle, reversals

topics.name: PARTNERSHIPS: ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
subtopics: Revise profitability (gross/net profit and operating indicators), liquidity (current and acid-test) and solvency indicators
Introduce stock turnover rate, stock holding period, average debtors' collection period, average creditors' payment period
Introduce risk/gearing (debt-equity ratio) and return on (average) partners' equity
topics.prior_knowledge: Gr 10 financial indicators; percentage and ratio arithmetic

topics.name: BUDGETING: BASIC CONCEPTS, CASH BUDGETS (DEBTORS’ COLLECTION AND CREDITORS’ PAYMENTS) AND PROJECTED STATEMENT OF COMPREHENSIVE INCOME (INCOME STATEMENT)
subtopics: Differentiate a cash budget from a projected income statement
Prepare and present a projected income statement (projected revenue and expenditure)
Prepare and present a cash budget for sole traders: projected receipts and payments, debtors' collection and creditors' payment schedules
Ethics, internal control and internal audit relating to budgeting and projections
topics.prior_knowledge: Gr 10 budget concepts and basic calculations; statement of comprehensive income; CRJ and CPJ

topics.name: INVENTORY SYSTEMS
subtopics: Perpetual vs periodic stock systems: differences, advantages, disadvantages
Cost of sales: perpetual (trading stock account and/or % mark-up) and periodic (opening stock, purchases, returns, carriage/customs, closing stock and/or mark-up)
Gross profit using sales, cost of sales and/or mark-up
Ethics, internal control and internal audit relating to stock
topics.prior_knowledge: Gr 10 perpetual-system content: trading stock, mark-up calculations, cost of sales, gross profit

topics.name: COST ACCOUNTING (MANUFACTURING): LEDGER ACCOUNTS AND CALCULATIONS
subtopics: Variable costs (direct material, direct labour, selling and distribution) and fixed costs (factory overheads, administration)
Unit cost and total cost of production; break-even point via contribution per unit
Stock ledger accounts: raw materials, work-in-progress, finished goods, consumable stores
Cost accounts: DMC, DLC, FOHC, administration, selling and distribution; related nominal accounts
Ethics, internal control and internal audit in a manufacturing environment
topics.prior_knowledge: Gr 10 cost concepts and basic cost calculations

topics.name: VALUE ADDED TAX (VAT)
subtopics: Need, purpose and principles of VAT; invoice or receipt base
VAT-able items, current (standard) rate, zero-rated and VAT-exempted items
Calculations: add VAT to cost-plus-mark-up; VAT from inclusive and exclusive amounts
Effect of bad debts, discounts and goods returned on VAT
VAT ethics and fraud; internal audit and control over VAT collection and payment to SARS
topics.prior_knowledge: General knowledge about tax and VAT
